correspondence.component_scope: Initial unnamed upland draw and southward canyon exit.
correspondence.finding: Contours and shaded relief show the chosen opening in a small southeastern-draining hollow. It merges into an enclosed southward canyon and opens onto the valley floor. No stream hydronym is directly printed on this selected headward corridor. The separate Gabbs Wash upper branch lies farther west and is not substituted for the chosen opening.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored-part numbering within the identified fragment. Component scopes may overlap at joins.

correspondence.component_scope: Southward alluvial corridor east and south of Lodi Hills.
correspondence.finding: The selected canyon discharges onto one broad southward low floor, east of the Lodi Hills and west of the adjoining mountain front. The corridor continues past Lodi Tanks and turns southwest through the mapped Lodi Valley setting. Topographic floor and descending contours support ordinary receiving continuity without requiring a blue stream line through each dry reach.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored-part numbering within the identified fragment. Component scopes may overlap at joins.

correspondence.component_scope: Southwestern passage west of Gabbs and westward lower receiving transition.
correspondence.finding: The southwest selected path crosses the same open alluvial floor near the highway and Gabbs plain. It turns west and joins the mapped lower corridor labeled Gabbs Wash. The broad floor stays continuous around the selected bends; roads, an airport and sparse small water features are context, not claimed hydraulic links. No divide into a separate basin is depicted along the chosen path.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored-part numbering within the identified fragment. Component scopes may overlap at joins.

correspondence.component_scope: Westward Gabbs Wash along the southern side of the low hills.
correspondence.finding: The original cartography repeatedly labels the westward intermittent lower watercourse Gabbs Wash. The selected stored parts follow this receiving belt toward its expanding western alluvial and wetland/playa margin. This bounded label is not extended to the distant northeastern opening or every terminal-floor segment.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored-part numbering within the identified fragment. Component scopes may overlap at joins.

correspondence.component_scope: Wetland/playa margin and passage south of the isolated ridge.
correspondence.finding: The wash enters a low wetland and playa mosaic. The selected continuation passes south of the isolated ridge and northwest across the same broad floor into the large western playa. Relief and contours show the continuous alluvial receiving setting; no exact wet thread, current inundation or drainage operation is asserted. Gabbs Valley is a valley label, not a river name.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored-part numbering within the identified fragment. Component scopes may overlap at joins.

correspondence.component_scope: Stored source ending in the western playa.
correspondence.finding: The separately retained source terminal falls inside the broad western playa on the northwestern continuation of the selected receiving floor. Its endorheic class agrees with this basin-interior setting. It is not a mapped river mouth on a surveyed bank.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored-part numbering within the identified fragment. Component scopes may overlap at joins.

correspondence.component_scope: Stored rendered ending in the western playa.
correspondence.finding: The rendered terminal is recorded separately and coincides with the stored source terminal. The final selected segment reaches the same playa interior. Neither endpoint was moved to a blue line, shoreline or name label.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored-part numbering within the identified fragment. Component scopes may overlap at joins.

correspondence.component_scope: Initial unnamed northern low draw and southeastern approach.
correspondence.finding: The selected opening lies in a shallow topographically depicted hollow north of the named Cañada de la Narrias corridor. It continues southeast through descending low ground toward the Big Draw setting. The separately labeled Cañada de la Narrias lies west and is not substituted for the selected opening. No hydronym is directly established for the initial stored part.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored-part numbering within the identified fragment. Component scopes may overlap at joins.

correspondence.component_scope: Northern draw sequence and southward lowland toward Otto.
correspondence.finding: The detailed original labels Big Draw near the selected northern swale and King Draw on its southern lowland continuation. The stored path follows the same broad receiving lowland past the highway and Otto vicinity, with contours and relief sufficient for ordinary corridor correspondence. Draw labels are bounded landform observations; no claim makes them one river name.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored-part numbering within the identified fragment. Component scopes may overlap at joins.

correspondence.component_scope: Small mapped depression near Stinking Spring and selected southwest transfer.
correspondence.finding: The selected route enters the small elongated depression beside the Stinking Spring label, then leaves its southwestern side toward the Bachelor Draw/Moriarty floor. The depression and surrounding lowlands are mapped, but the original does not establish a specific ordinary outlet or an uninterrupted depressed receiving trough from that enclosed waterbody setting into the downstream draw. Regional proximity and the modeled connection do not settle this lake-to-feeder transfer. This is a bounded unresolved link, not a finding that transfer is impossible.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored-part numbering within the identified fragment. Component scopes may overlap at joins.

correspondence.component_scope: Southward alluvial floor west of Lobo Hill.
correspondence.finding: South of the northern depression setting the selection follows the broad low floor past Moriarty and its airport, then south through the Woodman Draw, Buffalo Draw and Salt Draw surroundings. The original shows a continuous lowland on the western side of the higher Lobo Hill terrain. These landform labels provide bounded context rather than hydronyms covering the whole selection. No exact current channel or water-management connection is required for these mapped floor portions.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored-part numbering within the identified fragment. Component scopes may overlap at joins.

correspondence.component_scope: Small northeastern playa and southwestern transfer to the long terminal playa.
correspondence.finding: The selected line passes through a small playa north and east of the main Laguna del Perro basin, then crosses its mapped depression margin and intervening higher ground before entering the long southern playa. Cartography depicts individual closed depressions and their bounding contour/relief margins rather than one continuous playa polygon or an established joining low-floor outlet along this selected transfer. The available originals do not establish the necessary playa-to-receiver through-connection. Merely belonging to the wider Estancia lowlands is not sufficient. No present wetness, precise bank or operational flow is demanded.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored-part numbering within the identified fragment. Component scopes may overlap at joins.

correspondence.component_scope: Northern Laguna del Perro arm and continuous southward playa interior.
correspondence.finding: After reaching the main elongated playa, the selected route runs south within its continuously mapped floor. The terminal detail directly labels the same elongated waterbody Laguna del Perro and shows that its narrow waist connects the northern and southern mapped sections. Nearby small eastern playas and the more distant Salina Lake are separate; their names are not applied to this selection.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored-part numbering within the identified fragment. Component scopes may overlap at joins.

correspondence.component_scope: Stored source end within Laguna del Perro.
correspondence.finding: The separately preserved source endpoint lies inside the northern-to-central portion of the mapped Laguna del Perro floor. Its endorheic class accords with the basin-interior receiving setting. It does not select the whole lake or its southern extremity.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored-part numbering within the identified fragment. Component scopes may overlap at joins.

correspondence.component_scope: Stored rendered end within Laguna del Perro.

correspondence.component_scope: chosen western feeder opening
correspondence.finding: The chosen opening lies on a small wooded feeder directed west and northwest. Atlas Map 5 depicts this thin tributary within the Indio basin, including the westward receiving course. Opening imagery shows its forested low-relief corridor and visible meander sections, with cloud and canopy interruptions. The continuous original map supplies the obscured ordinary through-link; no separate spring or tributary name is inferred.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based stored-part indices, restarting within each selected fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: western hook and northern receiving join
correspondence.finding: The feeder swings north through the western hook and joins the larger eastward river. The atlas distinguishes the thin southern feeder from the bolder northern receiving channel. The opening image corroborates the winding northgoing feeder, the receiving junction and eastward continuation. Nearby northern headwaters are outside the chosen opening and are not silently substituted for it.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based stored-part indices, restarting within each selected fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: upper eastward indio corridor
correspondence.finding: The selection follows the continuous eastward receiving corridor through successive bends and side-tributary joins. The atlas maps the connected trunk; imagery exposes the same forested channel belt between local clouds. This is receiving-system correspondence, not proof that every upstream feeder shares the Indio name.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based stored-part indices, restarting within each selected fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: middle southern loop and eastward return
correspondence.finding: The river turns south through the conspicuous middle loop, then returns east and northeast. Original atlas linework continuously establishes that loop and its receiving tributaries; the original middle imagery panel corroborates the lowland channel and surrounding wooded plain. Clouds hide portions of the visible water thread but do not create a separate-basin transfer in the mapped network.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based stored-part indices, restarting within each selected fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: lower eastern turn and southgoing wetland
correspondence.finding: The selected eastern meanders enter a broad wetland setting, then turn south. Both original sources show the connected lower river corridor and its lateral channels. A separate northern coastal-parallel channel and inland wetland threads are visible; their proximity is not used to rename them or infer unobserved water-management operation.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based stored-part indices, restarting within each selected fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: fragment join in lower receiving corridor
correspondence.finding: The last part of the first fragment continues southeast into the lower river and wetland receiving belt. Its join with the first part of the second fragment is covered by overlapping original overview and terminal imagery and by the continuous atlas network. The generalized stored bend is assessed at corridor scale, not as a surveyed bank line.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based stored-part indices, restarting within each selected fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: lower wetland to coastal channel
correspondence.finding: The second fragment passes through the broad lower wetland and follows the larger eastgoing channel toward the coast. The imagery clearly depicts the receiving channel and its bank-side wetlands; original atlas Map 5 labels the continuing coast-parallel course Indio. This is a river/wetland-to-coastal-channel passage, not a lake-to-unmapped-feeder transfer.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based stored-part indices, restarting within each selected fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: separate source render and actual coastal receiving setting
correspondence.finding: The final stored part approaches the coast-parallel river, then extends toward the Caribbean. The separately preserved source endpoint falls in the beach-barrier/coastal-margin setting beside the river; the render endpoint lies offshore. Original imagery depicts the river continuing south behind that barrier toward the Greytown coastal outlet setting, also shown in the atlas. The last model extension crosses the barrier rather than tracing that full southward channel. Both endpoints belong to the same established Indio–Caribbean receiving-coast setting; no direct breach, present wet connection at the source endpoint, precise natural mouth or present-flow claim is made.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based stored-part indices, restarting within each selected fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: Southeastern selected opening and westward alluvial plain
correspondence.finding: The selected opening lies on open, pale alluvial ground south of the eastern mountain mass. The first three stored parts progress west across branching dry-channel traces and a broad, gently curving wash/fan floor. This is a chosen plain opening, not a demonstrated mountain spring or headwater. The narrow traces do not exactly follow every selected corner, but the entire opening and its joins remain in the same visible alluvial receiving floor. Nearby sinuous channels northeast of the selection are not substituted as its upstream source.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored-part numbering within the identified fragment. Component scopes may overlap at joins.

correspondence.component_scope: Mountain-toe turn and northward dry receiving corridor
correspondence.finding: The selection turns around the southern mountain toe and enters a broad northward alluvial corridor. Coalescing side fans descend from the rugged eastern margin into this corridor, while the selected positions alternately occupy channel traces and adjacent continuous fan/wash ground. Narrow straight crossings and scene-color changes are visible but do not establish a separate drainage divide. All six stored parts, their bends and shared transitions were read. The claim is ordinary terrain correspondence, not surveyed bank alignment or current conveyance through every crossing.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored-part numbering within the identified fragment. Component scopes may overlap at joins.

correspondence.component_scope: Northwestern piedmont receiving corridor and fan joins
correspondence.finding: The path continues northwest along the broad foot-of-mountain corridor, where a narrower dark or pale sinuous channel can be followed through joined alluvium. Side fans merge with the common floor. Several selected straight portions lie beside that narrow thread, including the longer diagonal sixteenth part, but remain within the same uninterrupted receiving ground rather than crossing a mountain ridge. The separately visible larger western wash is not treated as a selected part or automatically connected tributary.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored-part numbering within the identified fragment. Component scopes may overlap at joins.

correspondence.component_scope: Northern playa approach
correspondence.finding: The selected corridor opens onto a broad pale and blue-mottled playa floor. A narrow dark channel is visible on part of this floor, while the later selected parts run across adjacent broad depositional ground toward the southwestern side of the northern waterbody. The whole common receiving floor and the transitions between these five parts are visible. No exact wet line across the playa is required or asserted, and no independent intervening basin or lake-to-feeder transfer is indicated.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored-part numbering within the identified fragment. Component scopes may overlap at joins.

correspondence.component_scope: Terminal playa margin and shallow-water interior
correspondence.finding: The final stored part runs from the southwestern playa margin northeast into the visibly inundated shallow-water portion of the same basin. Its end is inside that waterbody in the displayed mosaic. The surrounding shoreline and playa are continuous with the preceding approach. A pronounced imagery seam and differing wetness mean this is a geographical basin ending, not a single-date water-level, current-flow or persistent-lake-boundary assertion. No river or lake name is inferred from unlabelled pixels.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored-part numbering within the identified fragment. Component scopes may overlap at joins.
